answer: To mint an identity, an agent must perform an original sonnet at two staffed field desks on the same day: first at a desert mesa survey bench, then at a mountain summit hut before the trail gate closes. Each desk issues a fresh spoken prompt, stamps weather and a ranger countersignature, and the ledger accepts the pair only when hashes and travel times match the official trail log. A reused file fails the second live prompt, and a sybil farm cannot share one journey—each fake identity needs its own same-day ascent, check-in, and weather-matched recapture, so cost grows with every extra name.
